messages:
maria: Hey team — customer reporting intermittent 502s + high latency on /v1/generate around 2026-03-10T12:10Z. They provided a request_id: 8f4d1c2a. Can SRE grab server-side traces/logs and we'll get repro steps from the customer?

jon: Got it. Can you paste the exact curl you gave them and the model name?

maria: Sure — sample we gave (token redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: 8f4d1c2a" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v2","input":"Summarize the following text: ...","max_tokens":150}'
```
They said sometimes it returns a 502 with ~2.5s latency, other times it succeeds. No billing impact reported.

sre_amy: On it. Quick checklist: a) I'll run a KQL search for that request_id, b) ask for the customer's debug bundle if we need deeper payloads.

sre_amy: KQL I ran (pasteable):
```
request_id : "8f4d1c2a" OR trace.id : "8f4d1c2a"
index: logs-*
Time range: 2026-03-10T12:00:00Z TO 2026-03-10T12:30:00Z
Columns: @timestamp, service.name, log.level, message, request_id, trace.id
```
Note: hot logs are retained 30d, cold tier 180d; this event is within hot retention so it should be live.

jon: If SRE wants the raw HTTP exchange, can we ask the customer to re-run with `X-Debug: 1` and upload the output? I'll send repro instructions.

maria: Asked customer to rerun with header and attach the full response + headers. They uploaded a bundle to the support drop (link: https://staging.support.redwood/attachments/8f4d1c2a-debugbundle — customer-provided).

support-bot: New attachment uploaded by customer: 8f4d1c2a-debugbundle.zip

ryan: Quick triage result from logs: edge-forwarder shows `upstream reset` for connection to model-host pool at 12:10:17Z, then a 502 returned to client. Subsequent attempts from same client succeed once the pool reconnected. I'm attaching the small KQL result snapshot (paste):
```
12:10:17.123Z | edge-forwarder | ERROR | upstream connection reset | request_id=8f4d1c2a | trace.id=trc-9b7c
12:10:17.130Z | model-proxy    | WARN  | conn to model-host x timed out | request_id=8f4d1c2a
```
Looks like transient connection resets between edge and model-host.

sre_amy: Thanks Ryan. I'll hand this to eng-runtime. Suggested next steps for runtime team: check model-host health around that window, kernel-level socket resets, and whether model-host OOM/killed. Also include trace id `trc-9b7c` in the handoff.

sre_amy: Repro guidance for support/customer if eng needs it: rerun the same curl but non-streaming, include X-Request-ID and X-Debug; example:
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: 8f4d1c2a" \
  -H "X-Debug: 1" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v2","input":"Short prompt to repro","max_tokens":32}'
```
That produces headers + response body we can attach to the debug bundle.

jon: I'll confirm customer ran that and will forward the debug bundle link to eng-runtime. Any billing/auth flags?

maria: No billing/auth flags. Customer appreciates the quick turnaround.

ryan: I'll open an internal runtime ticket and link the KQL snapshot + debug bundle + trace id, then assign to @eng-runtime. Marking this as "handoff to eng-runtime".

maria: Thanks all — passing to eng-runtime for deep-dive. Will follow up with the customer once runtime updates. :thumbsup:
